email.description:
Moderator email address used for authentication and communication. Must be unique across all moderators as defined by the unique constraint in the Prisma schema.

Validated against RFC 5322 email format standards and checked for uniqueness during account creation. This field serves as the primary contact method for system notifications and account recovery processes.

The email address must be verified before the moderator can access full administrative privileges, ensuring account security and preventing unauthorized access.

username.description:
Moderator username for display and identification within the discussion board platform. Must be unique across all moderators as enforced by the unique constraint in the Prisma schema.

Usernames serve as the primary identifier for moderator actions and are displayed alongside content moderation activities. The username must be alphanumeric and may include underscores or hyphens for readability.

This field supports moderator recognition by community members and provides accountability for moderation actions taken within the platform.

password.description:
Plain text password for moderator authentication that will be securely hashed before storage in the password_hash field. Must meet minimum security requirements including length and complexity.

The password undergoes secure hashing using industry-standard algorithms before being stored in the database. During authentication, the provided password is hashed and compared against the stored password_hash for verification.

Security measures include rate limiting, password strength validation, and secure transmission protocols to protect moderator credentials.

display_name.description:
Optional display name for moderator profile customization. Allows moderators to use a different name for public display while maintaining their unique username for authentication purposes.

The display name appears in moderator profile pages and may be shown alongside moderation actions where appropriate. This field supports personalization while maintaining the unique username constraint for authentication.

Display names can be changed without affecting authentication credentials, providing flexibility for moderator identity management.

bio.description:
Optional biography or description for moderator profile. Provides context about the moderator's role, expertise, or background to help community members understand their moderation approach.

The biography field supports rich text formatting and can include information about the moderator's experience, moderation philosophy, or areas of expertise. This helps build trust and transparency within the community.

Moderators can update their biography as their role evolves, maintaining current and relevant information for community members.

moderation_level.description:
Moderator privilege level indicating their administrative capabilities within the discussion board platform. Common levels include basic, senior, and admin, each with progressively broader moderation permissions.

The moderation level determines which administrative functions the moderator can access and what content management actions they can perform. Higher levels grant access to more sensitive moderation tools and system configuration options.

This field is assigned during account creation based on organizational policies and can be updated by system administrators as moderator responsibilities evolve.

ip.description:
Client IP address for session tracking and security monitoring. Optional field that can be provided for enhanced session security.

When provided, the IP address is recorded in the moderator session for audit purposes and security monitoring. The server can also extract this information from the request headers if not explicitly provided.

IP tracking helps detect suspicious registration patterns and enhances overall security for moderator account creation.

href.description:
Connection URL indicating the current page or application context from which the registration request originated.

This field is required for session context tracking and provides information about the registration source. It helps maintain session continuity and supports proper redirect behavior after account creation.

The URL should represent the actual page or application interface where the registration occurred.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL indicating the previous page that directed to the registration interface. Provides context about the registration flow and user navigation.

This field is required for comprehensive session tracking and helps understand the registration context. It supports analytics and security monitoring by tracking registration source patterns.

The referrer URL helps maintain proper navigation flow and supports post-registration redirect behavior.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.ICreate.description:
Request schema for creating a new discussion board moderator account with authentication credentials and profile information.

This schema defines the complete set of fields required and optional when registering a new moderator account. The schema ensures all necessary authentication and profile information is collected during the registration process while maintaining security best practices.

The creation process validates unique constraints for email and username fields, enforces password security requirements, and assigns appropriate moderation levels based on organizational policies. Successful registration creates a complete moderator profile ready for authentication and administrative duties.

Security considerations include proper validation of all input fields, secure handling of authentication credentials, and appropriate assignment of moderation privileges to maintain platform integrity and user trust.

email.description:
Moderator email address used for authentication and communication. Must be unique across all moderators and follows standard email format validation as defined in the Prisma schema.

This field is required for account recovery, system notifications, and administrative communications. The email address is verified during account setup to ensure authenticity and prevent unauthorized account creation.

The unique constraint ensures each moderator has a distinct identity within the system, supporting proper accountability and audit trail management for moderation activities.

username.description:
Moderator username for display and identification within the discussion board platform. Must be unique across all moderators and serves as the primary handle for moderator recognition.

Usernames are displayed alongside moderation actions and profile information, providing community members with consistent identification of moderators. The username remains immutable after account creation to maintain accountability.

This field supports the moderator's public identity within the community while the unique constraint prevents confusion and ensures clear attribution of moderation actions.

display_name.description:
Optional display name for moderator profile customization. Allows moderators to use a different name for public display while maintaining their unique username for authentication purposes.

Display names provide flexibility for moderator identity presentation without affecting authentication credentials. This field can be updated to reflect name changes or preferred public identification.

The display name appears in moderator profiles and may be shown in contexts where formal identification is preferred over the technical username, enhancing community engagement.

bio.description:
Optional biography or description for moderator profile. Provides context about the moderator's role, expertise, or background to help community members understand their moderation approach.

Biographies support transparency by allowing moderators to share information about their experience, moderation philosophy, or specific areas of expertise. This helps build trust and understanding within the community.

Rich text formatting supports detailed descriptions that can include moderator qualifications, community involvement history, or specific moderation focus areas, enhancing community-moderation relationships.

moderation_level.description:
Moderator privilege level indicating their administrative capabilities within the discussion board platform. Common levels include basic, senior, and admin, each with progressively broader moderation permissions.

The moderation level determines access to specific administrative functions, content management tools, and system configuration options. Higher levels grant authority over more sensitive moderation actions and platform settings.

This field is managed by system administrators and reflects the moderator's current responsibilities and trust level within the platform's administrative hierarchy.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the authenticated moderator account. Generated automatically during registration using UUID v4 and serves as the primary key for moderator records.

This identifier is used internally for database relationships and audit trail tracking. It remains constant throughout the moderator's account lifecycle, supporting consistent reference across all moderation activities and system logs.

The UUID format ensures global uniqueness and prevents identifier conflicts across distributed system instances, maintaining data integrity in multi-server environments.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the moderator account was created. Records the initial registration date and time for audit trail and account lifecycle tracking.

This field is automatically set during account creation and remains immutable throughout the account's existence. It supports account age verification, activity pattern analysis, and compliance with data retention policies.

The creation timestamp helps identify long-standing moderators and supports investigation of historical moderation activities through proper chronological context.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the moderator account was last updated. Tracks the most recent modification to the moderator profile for change management purposes.

This field is automatically updated whenever moderator profile information changes, providing a complete audit trail of account modifications. It helps identify recent changes and supports accountability for profile updates.

The update timestamp ensures accurate tracking of moderator activity patterns and supports investigation of suspicious account modifications or unauthorized changes.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp when the moderator account was soft deleted. Supports account recovery workflows while maintaining data integrity through soft deletion patterns.

When an account is soft deleted, this field is set to the deletion timestamp, allowing for potential account restoration while preventing active use. Hard deletion removes the record entirely from the system.

Soft deletion supports compliance with data retention requirements and provides a safety mechanism for accidental account termination, maintaining platform stability and user trust.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.IAuthorized.description:
Authorization response containing complete moderator identity information and authentication tokens for secure administrative access.

This schema represents the successful authentication response returned after moderator login or token refresh operations. It provides the moderator's complete profile information along with JWT tokens for continued API access to administrative functions.

The response enables moderators to perform their duties with proper authentication while maintaining accountability through complete identity disclosure. All timestamp fields support audit trail requirements and account lifecycle management.

Security considerations include proper token management, accurate identity information, and comprehensive audit trail support through immutable timestamp fields that track account creation, updates, and potential deletion status.

email_or_username.description:
Moderator's email address or username for authentication. Supports flexible login using either identifier as defined in the discussion_board_moderators schema.

The system validates this field against the unique email and username constraints in the database. Clients can provide either the registered email address or username for authentication convenience.

This flexibility accommodates different moderator preferences while maintaining security through proper credential validation.

password.description:
Moderator password for authentication verification. Must match the stored password_hash in the discussion_board_moderators table.

The password is transmitted securely and validated against the hashed version stored in the database. Proper password strength requirements are enforced during account creation.

Security measures include rate limiting, secure transmission, and proper error handling to prevent credential enumeration attacks.

ip.description:
Client IP address for session tracking and security monitoring. Optional field that can be provided for enhanced session security.

When provided, the IP address is recorded in the moderator session for audit purposes and security monitoring. The server can also extract this information from the request headers if not explicitly provided.

IP tracking helps detect suspicious login patterns and enhances overall security for moderator accounts.

href.description:
Connection URL indicating the current page or application context from which the login request originated.

This field is required for session context tracking and provides information about the login source. It helps maintain session continuity and supports proper redirect behavior after authentication.

The URL should represent the actual page or application interface where the login occurred.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL indicating the previous page that directed to the login interface. Provides context about the login flow and user navigation.

This field is required for comprehensive session tracking and helps understand the authentication context. It supports analytics and security monitoring by tracking login source patterns.

The referrer URL helps maintain proper navigation flow and supports post-authentication redirect behavior.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.ILogin.description:
Moderator login credentials for authentication.

Contains the necessary information to authenticate a moderator account, including flexible identifier support (email or username) and password verification. The request includes session context information for security tracking.

This DTO enables secure moderator authentication while providing session context for enhanced security monitoring and audit capabilities. Successful authentication returns JWT tokens for API access.

The schema maps to the discussion_board_moderators Prisma model for field validation and ensures all authentication data aligns with the database structure. Security considerations include credential validation, session tracking, and proper error handling to prevent information leakage.

refresh_token.description: Valid refresh token used to obtain new access and refresh tokens. This token must be previously issued by the authentication system and not expired or revoked.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.IRefresh.description:
Refresh token request for moderator authentication renewal.

This schema represents the request body for refreshing moderator JWT tokens. It contains the refresh token that was previously issued during authentication and is used to obtain new access and refresh tokens without requiring re-authentication.

The refresh token mechanism allows moderators to maintain extended sessions while maintaining security through regular token rotation. The token must be valid, unexpired, and not revoked to successfully generate new tokens.

The schema maps to the discussion_board_moderators Prisma model for proper session management and token validation. This ensures that refresh operations maintain security integrity while providing seamless session continuity for moderator administrative activities.

page.description: Page number for pagination, starting from 1. Used to navigate through large result sets efficiently.

limit.description: Number of items per page, with maximum limit of 100 to ensure optimal performance and prevent excessive data transfer.

search.description: Search term to filter channels by name or description content. Supports partial matching and case-insensitive text search across channel metadata.

Inactive channels temporarily disabled from user interaction.
Archived channels preserved for historical reference but no longer accepting new content.

Descending order from largest to smallest values.

created_before.description: Filter channels created before this specific date and time for historical context.

IDiscussionBoardChannel.IRequest.description:
Search and filter parameters for discussion board channel retrieval operations.

This schema defines comprehensive request parameters for querying discussion board channels with advanced filtering capabilities. It supports pagination, text search, status-based filtering, date range queries, and multiple sorting options to efficiently retrieve relevant channel information.

The parameters are designed to work with the discussion_board_channels table structure, allowing precise control over result sets while maintaining system performance through sensible defaults and constraints.

id.description: Unique identifier for the discussion board channel. Automatically generated UUID v4 that serves as the primary key for channel operations.

name.description: Display name identifying the channel's broad topic category such as Economics, Politics, or Technology. Used for user navigation and content organization.

description.description: Brief explanatory text describing the channel's purpose, discussion scope, and community guidelines. Helps users understand the channel's focus before participating.

status.description: Operational status indicating whether the channel is active (accepting content), inactive (temporarily disabled), or archived (preserved for reference).

created_at.description: Timestamp when the channel was originally created in the system. Useful for chronological sorting and activity analysis.

IDiscussionBoardChannel.ISummary.description:
Summary view of discussion board channels optimized for list displays and browsing operations.

Provides essential channel information for efficient navigation and selection within the discussion board interface. This summary format includes only the most critical fields needed for channel identification and basic status assessment.

The schema maintains a direct relationship with the discussion_board_channels Prisma model, ensuring data consistency and accurate representation of channel entities across the application.

id.description:
Primary key identifier for the discussion board channel. Generated automatically using UUID v4 format upon channel creation. This identifier remains immutable throughout the channel's lifecycle and serves as the primary reference for all channel-related operations.

The UUID format ensures global uniqueness and prevents identifier conflicts across distributed systems. This field is system-managed and cannot be modified by users or administrators.

name.description:
Channel name that identifies the discussion category (e.g., 'Economics', 'Politics'). This name must be unique across all discussion board channels and serves as the primary human-readable identifier for the channel.

Channel names follow specific naming conventions and are validated for uniqueness during creation. Once set, channel names cannot be modified to maintain stable references throughout the system and prevent breaking existing content relationships.

description.description:
Detailed description explaining the channel's purpose and discussion scope. This field provides comprehensive context about what types of content belong in this channel and how it fits within the broader discussion board ecosystem.

The description helps users understand the channel's focus area and guides content creators in selecting appropriate channels for their posts. Administrators can update this description to reflect evolving channel purposes or community guidelines.

status.description:
Channel status indicating whether it is active, inactive, or archived. Active channels are visible to users and accept new content, while inactive channels remain visible but prevent new posts. Archived channels are hidden from general view but preserved for historical reference.

Status changes are managed by administrators to control channel availability and content flow. Each status level has specific implications for content visibility, posting permissions, and administrative workflows.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the channel was created. This system-managed field records the exact date and time when the channel was first established in the discussion board platform.

The creation timestamp provides audit trail information and helps administrators track channel lifecycle. This field is immutable and cannot be modified after creation.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the channel was last updated. This system-managed field automatically records the date and time whenever channel properties are modified, providing a comprehensive audit trail of changes.

The update timestamp helps administrators track channel modifications and maintain version history. This field is automatically managed by the system.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp when the channel was soft deleted, if applicable. This field supports soft deletion functionality, allowing channels to be marked as deleted while preserving their data for potential recovery or archival purposes.

When a channel is soft deleted, this timestamp is set to indicate the deletion time. If the channel is active, this field remains null. Soft deletion allows for content preservation while removing channels from active use.

IDiscussionBoardChannel.description:
Discussion board channels that categorize content by broad topics such as Economics and Politics.

Each channel represents a major discussion category that contains multiple sections. Channels define the primary organizational structure of the discussion board and determine how content is grouped and displayed to users. The channel entity maintains comprehensive metadata including name, description, status, and timestamps to support content organization and administrative management.

Channels can be activated or deactivated by administrators to control which topics are available for discussion. Each channel maintains its own configuration settings and moderation policies, allowing for customized content management approaches based on topic-specific requirements.

The channel entity integrates with the discussion_board_channels table in the Prisma schema, ensuring data consistency and supporting all CRUD operations through the API layer. Channels serve as the foundation for content organization, user navigation, and administrative oversight throughout the discussion board platform.

name.description:
Channel name that identifies the discussion category (e.g., 'Economics', 'Politics'). This name must be unique across all discussion board channels and serves as the primary human-readable identifier for the channel.

Channel names follow specific naming conventions and are validated for uniqueness during creation. The name must be provided during channel creation and cannot be modified afterward to maintain stable system references.

description.description:
Detailed description explaining the channel's purpose and discussion scope. This field provides comprehensive context about what types of content belong in this channel and how it fits within the broader discussion board ecosystem.

The description helps users understand the channel's focus area and guides content creators in selecting appropriate channels for their posts. This information is essential for establishing clear content categorization from the channel's inception.

status.description:
Channel status indicating whether it is active, inactive, or archived. This field determines the initial availability of the channel upon creation, allowing administrators to create channels in different states based on deployment strategy.

The status can be configured to immediately activate the channel for user access or keep it inactive for future activation. This flexibility supports various channel management workflows and deployment scenarios.

IDiscussionBoardChannel.ICreate.description:
Data required to create a new discussion board channel.

This DTO contains all the necessary information to establish a new channel in the discussion board system. Channel names must be unique across the entire platform to prevent conflicts and ensure clear content organization. The creation process validates name uniqueness and applies appropriate naming conventions to maintain system integrity.

The status field determines the initial availability of the channel, allowing administrators to create channels in inactive state for future activation or immediately active for immediate user access. This DTO excludes system-managed fields such as identifiers and timestamps, which are automatically generated during the creation process.

This schema integrates with the discussion_board_channels table as defined in the Prisma schema, ensuring that all required fields for channel creation are properly specified and validated before persistence.

name.description: Channel name that identifies the discussion category (e.g., 'Economics', 'Politics'). Immutable field that cannot be updated after creation as it serves as the stable identifier for the channel.

description.description: Detailed description explaining the channel's purpose and discussion scope.

status.description: Channel status indicating whether it is active, inactive, or archived.

IDiscussionBoardChannel.IUpdate.description:
Data transfer object for updating existing discussion board channels.

This DTO allows administrators to modify channel properties while preserving immutable fields like the channel name and creation timestamp. Only modifiable fields are included to prevent accidental changes to system-managed data.

Channel names cannot be updated as they serve as stable identifiers throughout the system, maintaining referential integrity with existing content and sections. The name field is included as immutable to provide context but cannot be modified through update operations.

This DTO supports partial updates where administrators can modify individual properties without requiring all fields to be provided. All fields are optional to enable targeted modifications while maintaining data consistency.

id.description: Primary Key.

name.description: Section name that identifies the specific topic within the parent channel.

description.description: Detailed description explaining the section's specific focus and discussion guidelines.

status.description: Section status indicating whether it is active, inactive, or archived.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the section was created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the section was last updated.

IDiscussionBoardSection.description:
Sections within discussion board channels that provide finer content organization.

Sections allow administrators to create subcategories within channels for more specific topic organization. For example, an Economics channel might have sections for 'Monetary Policy', 'Fiscal Policy', and 'International Trade'.

Sections inherit the parent channel's configuration and moderation settings but can have section-specific overrides. Users can browse content by section to find discussions on specific topics.

This entity represents a composition relationship where the parent channel owns its sections. The section maintains its own lifecycle with creation and update timestamps for audit purposes.

Sections support soft deletion through status management rather than physical deletion, allowing for content preservation and potential restoration while maintaining referential integrity with related posts and comments.

name.description: Section name that identifies the specific topic within the parent channel. Must be unique within the parent channel scope to prevent duplicate sections. The name should clearly indicate the section's focus and topic area for easy user navigation.

description.description: Detailed description explaining the section's specific focus, discussion guidelines, and intended content scope. This description helps users understand what types of discussions are appropriate for this section and sets expectations for content quality and relevance.

channel.description: Parent discussion board channel that contains this section. The channel provides the organizational context and broad topic category for the section. Sections are scoped to their parent channels and inherit channel-level configuration settings.

IDiscussionBoardSection.ICreate.description:
Data transfer object for creating new discussion board sections within existing channels.

Contains the essential information required to establish a new section with proper organizational context and content guidelines. The section name must be unique within the parent channel to prevent duplicate sections and maintain clear content organization.

The channel reference establishes the parent-child relationship between sections and channels, ensuring proper scoping and inheritance of channel-level settings. Sections inherit moderation policies, access controls, and configuration settings from their parent channels.

Used in section creation operations where administrators need to establish new organizational structures within existing discussion board channels. The DTO focuses on user-provided data while excluding system-managed fields like status, timestamps, and identifiers.

IDiscussionBoardSection.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying discussion board section properties while maintaining organizational relationships.

This DTO allows administrators to modify section properties such as name, description, and channel assignment while preserving the section's content and user interactions. All fields are optional to support partial updates without requiring complete section reconfiguration.

The channel field allows section reassignment between different channels when organizational restructuring is needed. Name and description updates help maintain section relevance and clarity as discussion topics evolve over time.

Security considerations include requiring moderator privileges for section modifications. The operation ensures data integrity by preserving section content and user interactions throughout the update process while allowing administrators to refine section organization and focus.

Used in section update operations where administrators need to adapt section properties to changing discussion needs without disrupting existing content or user engagement patterns.

name.description: Updated section name that identifies the specific topic within the parent channel. Must remain unique within the parent channel scope to prevent naming conflicts after modification.

description.description: Updated detailed description explaining the section's revised focus, discussion guidelines, and content scope. Helps maintain section relevance as discussion topics and community needs evolve.

channel.description: Updated parent discussion board channel assignment for organizational restructuring. Allows moving sections between channels when topic categorization needs adjustment.

id.description: Unique identifier for the discussion board section. Generated automatically using UUID v4 format for global uniqueness and security.

name.description: Section name that identifies the specific topic within the parent channel. Must be unique within the channel and provides the primary identification for navigation and content organization.

description.description: Brief description explaining the section's specific focus and discussion guidelines. Helps users understand the scope and purpose of the section before engaging with content.

status.description: Section status indicating whether it is active, inactive, or archived. Active sections are available for content creation and discussion, inactive sections are temporarily disabled, and archived sections preserve historical content without new activity.

channel.description: Parent channel that contains this section. Provides essential context for navigation and organizational structure, linking the section to its broader topic category.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the section was created. Useful for sorting sections by creation date in list displays and tracking section lifecycle.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the section was last updated. Tracks modifications to section properties such as name, description, or status changes.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when the section was soft deleted, if applicable. Supports soft deletion functionality while preserving historical data integrity.

IDiscussionBoardSection.ISummary.description:
Summary view of discussion board sections for list displays and browsing operations.

Provides essential information for section browsing and selection, including the parent channel context for navigation purposes. This summary includes key metadata for efficient list rendering while maintaining referential integrity with the parent channel.

Optimized for paginated list operations where users need to browse sections within specific channels, with support for sorting by creation date and filtering by status. The summary excludes detailed content and large text fields to ensure optimal performance in list views.

Used primarily in section listing operations where users need to select sections within channels for content creation or browsing. The summary maintains relationships with parent channels while providing sufficient information for user decision-making.

page.description: Page number for paginated results, starting from 1. Controls which subset of results is returned based on the configured page size.

limit.description: Number of items per page for paginated results. Determines how many sections are returned in a single response, with a maximum limit of 100 for performance optimization.

search.description: Search term to filter sections by name or description. Supports partial matching and case-insensitive text search across section metadata.

oneOf.description: Filter sections by specific status (active, inactive, archived). Allows administrators to retrieve sections based on their current operational state for workflow management.
Filter sections by specific status (active, inactive, archived). Allows administrators to retrieve sections based on their current operational state for workflow management.
Filter sections by specific status (active, inactive, archived). Allows administrators to retrieve sections based on their current operational state for workflow management.

status.description: Filter sections by specific status (active, inactive, archived). Allows administrators to retrieve sections based on their current operational state for workflow management.

IDiscussionBoardSection.IRequest.description:
Query parameters for searching and filtering discussion board sections with pagination support.

This DTO supports paginated retrieval of sections with comprehensive filtering capabilities. The search parameter allows text-based filtering across section names and descriptions using partial matching algorithms.

Status filtering enables administrators to retrieve sections based on their current operational state, supporting workflow management and content organization tasks. Pagination ensures efficient data retrieval for large section collections.

The request parameters are designed to work together, allowing users to combine search terms with status filters while maintaining pagination controls. This provides flexible section discovery and management capabilities for both users and administrators.

title.description: Post title summarizing the discussion topic.

content.description: Main content body of the post supporting Markdown formatting.

status.description: Current status of the post: draft, published, archived, or deleted.

is_pinned.description: Whether the post is pinned to the top of the discussion board.

is_locked.description: Whether the post is locked from further comments.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the post was last updated.

published_at.description: Timestamp when the post was published and made visible to users.

archived_at.description: Timestamp when the post was archived due to age or inactivity.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when the post was soft-deleted.

IDiscussionBoardPost.description:
Main discussion posts created by members or moderators.

Represents the primary content entities that form discussion threads on the economic/political discussion board. Each post contains a title, content body, and optional attachments. Posts are organized by channels and sections to categorize discussions by topic.

Posts support various statuses including draft, published, and archived states to manage content lifecycle. Authors can edit their posts within a limited timeframe, and the system maintains edit history for moderation purposes.

IDiscussionBoardPost.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering DTO for discussion board posts with pagination support.

This DTO provides comprehensive search capabilities for finding discussion board posts across the platform. It supports filtering by various criteria including title keywords, content search, post status, channel association, section categorization, actor type, and date ranges.

The DTO integrates with the discussion_board_posts table structure and its relationships to channels and sections. It supports pagination with configurable page sizes and multiple sorting options including creation date, update date, title, and pin status.

Security considerations include channel-based access control where users can only search posts within channels they have permission to access. The operation validates that specified channels exist and are active before returning results.

Used in post search operations where users need to filter and browse discussion content based on multiple criteria with proper pagination controls.

limit.description: Number of items per page for pagination (maximum 100).

search.description: Search term for filtering posts by title or content keywords.

discussion_board_channel_id.description: Filter posts by specific discussion board channel.

discussion_board_section_id.description: Filter posts by specific section within a channel.

actor_type.description: Filter posts by actor type: member or moderator.

status.description: Filter posts by status: draft, published, archived, or deleted.

created_before.description: Filter posts created before this timestamp.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the content being reported in moderation workflows. Uses UUID v4 format for global uniqueness and security.

This identifier links back to the original content entity (post, comment, or member profile) that is subject to moderation review.
The ID ensures precise content targeting and prevents ambiguity in moderation actions.

type.description:
Type of content being reported, categorizing the moderation target for workflow routing.

Supported values include 'post' for discussion board posts, 'comment' for threaded comments, and 'member_profile' for user profile content.
This classification enables efficient moderation queue assignment and specialized handling procedures based on content category.

title.description:
Title or summary description of the content being reported, providing essential context for moderation decisions.

For posts, this represents the post title; for comments, a summary of the comment content; for profiles, the member's display name.
This field enables moderators to quickly assess content context without needing to access the full content body during initial review.

IDiscussionBoardPost.ISummary.description:
Summary view of content for moderation reporting and reference purposes.

Provides essential identification and context for content being reported in moderation workflows, optimized for efficient display in moderation interfaces while maintaining complete content context.

This summary DTO enables rapid content identification and categorization during moderation queue processing, supporting quick decision-making while preserving audit trail integrity.

Used primarily in content report creation and moderation dashboard displays where full content details are not immediately required but basic identification is essential for workflow management.

id.description:
Primary key identifier for the configuration setting.

Unique identifier automatically generated by the system to ensure each configuration setting has a distinct identity. Used for internal reference and relationship management within the database.

config_key.description:
Unique identifier key for the configuration setting.

This key serves as the human-readable identifier for the configuration setting (e.g., 'max_attachment_size', 'post_moderation_enabled'). Each key must be unique across the entire configuration system to prevent conflicts and ensure consistent behavior.

The key follows a naming convention that describes the setting's purpose and scope, making it easily identifiable by administrators and developers.

config_value.description:
Value associated with the configuration key.

Stores the actual setting value as a string for maximum flexibility. The interpretation of this value depends on the config_type field, which specifies how the value should be processed (boolean, number, string, json).

For boolean values, this field should contain 'true' or 'false'. For numeric values, it should contain the number as a string. For JSON values, it should contain valid JSON syntax.

config_type.description:
Data type specification for the configuration value.

Indicates how the config_value field should be interpreted and processed. Valid types include:
- 'boolean': True/false values
- 'number': Numeric values
- 'string': Text values
- 'json': Complex structured data

This field ensures proper type validation and prevents type mismatches when configuration values are used throughout the system.

description.description:
Human-readable description of the configuration setting.

Provides context and documentation about the purpose, usage, and impact of this configuration setting. This description helps administrators understand what the setting controls and how changes might affect system behavior.

Should be clear, concise, and informative to support effective configuration management.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the configuration setting was created.

Records the exact date and time when this configuration setting was first added to the system. This audit trail helps track configuration changes and understand the evolution of system settings over time.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the configuration setting was last modified.

Tracks the most recent modification to this configuration setting. This field is automatically updated whenever changes are made, providing a complete history of configuration modifications for audit and troubleshooting purposes.

IDiscussionBoardConfiguration.description:
Discussion board configuration entity representing system-wide settings and parameters.

This entity stores platform configuration settings that control various aspects of the discussion board system behavior, including moderation policies, attachment limits, content guidelines, and system customization options. Each configuration has a unique key-value pair with type specification and descriptive documentation.

Configuration settings are managed by authorized administrators and moderators who can create, update, and maintain system parameters without requiring code changes. The system uses these configurations to dynamically adjust behavior based on organizational needs and platform requirements.

Security considerations include access controls to prevent unauthorized modification of critical system settings. Configuration changes can significantly impact platform stability and user experience, so modification privileges are restricted to trusted administrative roles.

page.description:
Page number for paginated configuration results retrieval.

Specifies which page of configuration settings to retrieve, starting from page 1. Each page contains a configurable number of configuration records based on the limit parameter.

Used in conjunction with limit to implement efficient pagination for browsing large configuration sets. The system automatically calculates total pages based on record count and page size.

limit.description:
Maximum number of configuration records to return per page.

Controls the page size for configuration listing operations. The system enforces a maximum limit of 100 records per page to prevent excessive resource consumption and ensure optimal performance.

Smaller limits improve response times for clients that don't require the full configuration set at once, while larger limits reduce the number of API calls needed for complete configuration retrieval.

search.description:
Search term for filtering configurations by key patterns or description content.

Performs case-insensitive pattern matching across configuration keys and descriptions. Useful for quickly locating specific settings among potentially hundreds of system configurations.

Supports partial matching, allowing administrators to find configurations using keywords or phrases without needing exact key names.

config_type_filter.description:
Filter to restrict results to configurations of a specific data type.

Valid options include 'boolean', 'number', 'string', and 'json'. This parameter helps administrators focus on configurations that share similar value types and processing requirements.

When omitted, configurations of all types are included in the results, providing a comprehensive view of all system settings.

oneOf.description:
Sort configurations alphabetically by their unique identifier keys.

Useful for organizing configurations in a predictable alphabetical order, making it easier to locate specific settings by their key names.

Sort configurations by their creation timestamp, showing newest configurations first.

Helps administrators identify recently added configuration settings and track the evolution of system parameters over time.

Sort configurations by their last modification timestamp, showing most recently updated settings first.

Useful for identifying configurations that have been recently changed, which may require additional review or testing.

order_by.description:
Field selection for sorting configuration search results.

Determines the primary sorting criteria for returned configurations. Available options include alphabetical sorting by configuration key or chronological sorting by creation or modification dates.

This parameter helps organize configuration listings in a meaningful way that supports efficient administrative review and management workflows.

oneOf.description:
Sort configurations in ascending order.

For alphabetical sorting, this means A-Z order. For date sorting, this means oldest to newest.

Useful for chronological analysis or when a specific ordering sequence is required.

Sort configurations in descending order.

For alphabetical sorting, this means Z-A order. For date sorting, this means newest to oldest.

Typically used with date fields to show most recent configurations first, which is often the most relevant view for administrative tasks.

order_direction.description:
Direction specification for configuration sorting.

Determines whether configurations are sorted in ascending (A-Z, oldest-first) or descending (Z-A, newest-first) order.

When combined with order_by, this parameter provides flexible sorting capabilities that can be tailored to specific administrative needs and workflows.

IDiscussionBoardConfiguration.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering criteria for retrieving discussion board configuration settings.

This request DTO provides comprehensive search capabilities for configuration management operations, allowing administrators to filter, sort, and paginate system configuration settings efficiently.

Supported filtering options include keyword search across configuration keys and descriptions, type-based filtering for specific data types, and flexible sorting by key, creation date, or modification date.

Pagination parameters ensure that large configuration sets can be managed effectively without overwhelming clients or servers. All parameters are optional, allowing clients to request configurations with varying levels of specificity based on their current administrative needs.

The DTO integrates with the discussion_board_configurations table structure, supporting all available configuration fields while maintaining performance and security considerations appropriate for system administration operations.

config_key.description:
Unique identifier key for the new configuration setting.

Must be globally unique across all system configurations. Follows naming conventions that clearly describe the setting's purpose and scope (e.g., 'max_attachment_size', 'post_moderation_enabled', 'user_registration_enabled').

This key will be used throughout the system to reference and apply the configuration setting, so it should be descriptive yet concise for easy identification and management.

config_value.description:
Initial value for the configuration setting, stored as a string for maximum flexibility.

The interpretation of this value depends on the specified config_type:
- For 'boolean' type: Use 'true' or 'false'
- For 'number' type: Provide numeric value as string (e.g., '100', '3.14')
- For 'string' type: Provide text content directly
- For 'json' type: Provide valid JSON syntax

This flexible approach allows the system to handle various configuration types while maintaining a consistent storage format.

config_type.description:
Data type specification that determines how the config_value should be interpreted.

Valid options include 'boolean', 'number', 'string', and 'json'. This field ensures proper validation and processing of configuration values throughout the system.

The type specification prevents type mismatches and ensures that configuration values are used correctly in different parts of the application, maintaining system stability and predictable behavior.

description.description:
Comprehensive human-readable description explaining the configuration's purpose, usage, and impact.

Should clearly describe what system behavior this setting controls, how changes affect platform functionality, and any important considerations when modifying the value.

Provides essential context for administrators to make informed decisions about configuration changes and understand the potential consequences of modifications to system settings.

IDiscussionBoardConfiguration.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating new discussion board configuration settings.

This DTO contains all necessary information to establish a new system configuration parameter that controls various aspects of platform behavior, including moderation policies, attachment limits, content guidelines, and system customization options.

Each configuration requires a unique key identifier, appropriate value with type specification, and comprehensive description to support effective configuration management. The system validates configuration key uniqueness and value-type compatibility before creating the new setting.

Security considerations include restricting this operation to authorized administrators only, as configuration settings control critical system behavior that can significantly impact platform stability, security, and user experience. System-generated fields like id, created_at, and updated_at are automatically populated and should not be included in creation requests.

config_value.description:
Updated value for the configuration setting.

If provided, replaces the existing configuration value. Must conform to the existing config_type of the configuration setting. For boolean values, use 'true' or 'false'. For numeric values, provide the number as a string. For JSON values, provide valid JSON syntax.

The system validates that the new value is compatible with the configuration's data type. If config_type is also being updated, the validation will use the new type specification. This ensures data integrity and prevents type mismatches that could cause system instability.

config_type.description:
Updated data type specification for the configuration value.

If provided, changes how the config_value is interpreted. Valid options: 'boolean', 'number', 'string', 'json'. Changing the config_type may require corresponding changes to the config_value to ensure compatibility.

The system validates that the new config_type is supported and that the existing config_value can be converted to the new type if necessary. This prevents configuration errors and maintains system stability during configuration updates.

description.description:
Updated human-readable description of the configuration setting.

If provided, replaces the existing description. Should clearly explain the configuration's purpose, usage, and any important considerations for administrators.

The description should be comprehensive enough to help administrators understand the impact of configuration changes on system behavior. This documentation is crucial for effective configuration management and troubleshooting.

IDiscussionBoardConfiguration.IUpdate.description:
Request DTO for updating existing discussion board configuration settings.

This DTO allows partial updates to configuration settings. Only the fields provided will be modified; omitted fields retain their current values. This enables flexible configuration management without requiring complete re-specification of all settings.

The config_key field is provided as a URL path parameter and MUST NOT be duplicated in the request body to prevent security vulnerabilities. System-generated fields like id, created_at, and updated_at are managed automatically and cannot be modified through this DTO.

Security considerations: This operation requires moderator privileges. The system validates that configuration keys exist and that updated values conform to the specified type (or new type if config_type is modified). Rate limiting should be implemented to prevent abuse of configuration modification capabilities.

id.description:
Primary key identifier for the configuration setting.

Unique identifier automatically generated by the system to ensure each configuration setting has a distinct identity. Used for internal reference and relationship management within the database.

This UUID serves as the immutable identifier for the configuration record throughout its lifecycle, providing a stable reference point for audit trails and system integrations.

config_key.description:
Unique identifier key for the configuration setting.

This key serves as the human-readable identifier for the configuration setting (e.g., 'max_attachment_size', 'post_moderation_enabled'). Each key must be unique across the entire configuration system to prevent conflicts and ensure consistent behavior.

The key follows a naming convention that describes the setting's purpose and scope, making it easily identifiable by administrators and developers. This field is indexed for efficient lookup operations.

config_value.description:
Value associated with the configuration key.

Stores the actual setting value as a string for maximum flexibility. The interpretation of this value depends on the config_type field, which specifies how the value should be processed (boolean, number, string, json).

For boolean values, this field should contain 'true' or 'false'. For numeric values, it should contain the number as a string. For JSON values, it should contain valid JSON syntax. The system performs type validation when configurations are used.

config_type.description:
Data type specification for the configuration value.

Indicates how the config_value field should be interpreted and processed. Valid types include:
- 'boolean': True/false values
- 'number': Numeric values
- 'string': Text values
- 'json': Complex structured data

This field ensures proper type validation and prevents type mismatches when configuration values are used throughout the system. It maintains data integrity across configuration operations.

description.description:
Human-readable description of the configuration setting.

Provides context and documentation about the purpose, usage, and impact of this configuration setting. This description helps administrators understand what the setting controls and how changes might affect system behavior.

Should be clear, concise, and informative to support effective configuration management. This documentation is essential for maintaining configuration consistency across administrative changes.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the configuration setting was created.

Records the exact date and time when this configuration setting was first added to the system. This audit trail helps track configuration changes and understand the evolution of system settings over time.

This field is automatically set when the configuration is created and provides historical context for configuration management and troubleshooting activities.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the configuration setting was last modified.

Tracks the most recent modification to this configuration setting. This field is automatically updated whenever changes are made, providing a complete history of configuration modifications for audit and troubleshooting purposes.

The updated_at field helps administrators identify when configurations were last changed and track the configuration lifecycle for compliance and maintenance purposes.

IDiscussionBoardConfiguration.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of discussion board configuration settings.

Provides essential information about platform-wide configuration parameters that control system behavior, moderation policies, and content guidelines. These settings are managed by administrators and affect how the discussion board operates.

The summary includes all configuration fields to provide complete information for configuration management interfaces. This comprehensive representation ensures administrators have access to all necessary details when reviewing and managing system configurations.

Security considerations: Configuration summaries are accessible to authorized administrators and moderators. Sensitive configuration values should be handled appropriately based on the configuration's purpose and potential impact on system security.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when the guest account was soft deleted. Can be set to null to restore a deleted guest account. This is the only field that can be meaningfully updated for guest accounts.

IDiscussionBoardGuest.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for guest users allowing modification of guest account status.

This DTO allows updating the soft deletion status of guest accounts. The deleted_at field can be modified to manage guest account lifecycle - setting it to a timestamp marks the account as deleted, while setting it to null restores a previously deleted account.

System-managed fields like id, guest_token, created_at, and updated_at are excluded as they are managed automatically by the system or are immutable identifiers. The guest_token field serves as the permanent identifier and cannot be changed after creation.

This DTO provides the primary update functionality for guest management operations, focusing exclusively on account lifecycle management through the deleted_at field.

id.description: Primary Key.

guest_token.description: Unique anonymous identifier for guest tracking without authentication requirements.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the guest account was created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the guest account was last updated.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when the guest account was soft deleted.

IDiscussionBoardGuest.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of guest user accounts.

Provides essential information about anonymous users who can browse content without authentication. Guest accounts serve as temporary identifiers for users exploring the platform before committing to registration.

This summary includes the guest token and timestamps for tracking guest activity and managing guest-to-member transitions. It provides a lightweight representation suitable for list views and guest management interfaces while maintaining all relevant guest account information.

The summary excludes detailed guest session information to maintain efficiency in list operations. Guest accounts can be tracked through their unique guest_token identifier and lifecycle timestamps for effective guest management.

pagination.description: Pagination parameters for controlling result sets and page navigation

search.description:
Search term for filtering guest tokens by partial matching. Supports case-insensitive substring search for flexible guest account identification.

Empty or null values disable search filtering, allowing for broad guest account queries without text constraints.

created_after.description:
Filter guests created after this timestamp for chronological analysis of guest registration patterns.

Enables date-range queries to track guest account creation trends and platform growth metrics over specific time periods.

created_before.description:
Filter guests created before this timestamp, complementing created_after for precise date-range filtering.

Combined with created_after, enables bounded time period queries for comprehensive guest activity reporting and analytics.

oneOf.description: Sort by guest account creation timestamp for chronological ordering of results.
Sort by guest account last update timestamp for recent activity-based ordering.
Sort by guest token value for alphabetical or identifier-based ordering.

sort_by.description:
Field to sort results by, determining the primary ordering criteria for paginated guest lists.

Supported sorting fields include creation timestamp, update timestamp, and guest token for flexible result organization based on different use cases.

oneOf.description: Ascending sort order returning oldest records first based on the selected sort_by field.
Descending sort order returning newest records first based on the selected sort_by field.

order.description:
Sorting direction controlling whether results are returned in ascending or descending order.

Ascending order returns records from oldest to newest, while descending order returns from newest to oldest based on the sort_by field selection.

IDiscussionBoardGuest.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering criteria for discussion board guest account queries.

This request DTO provides comprehensive filtering capabilities for administrative guest management operations. It supports pagination through a unified pagination object, text search for guest token matching, date-range filtering for temporal analysis, and flexible sorting options.

The combination of search parameters enables precise targeting of guest accounts based on creation patterns, identifier characteristics, and temporal attributes. Empty or null values for optional parameters disable the corresponding filters, allowing for broad queries when specific filtering is not required.

This schema integrates with guest search operations to deliver filtered, paginated results while maintaining consistent pagination patterns across the API. The design supports both simple paginated queries and complex multi-criteria searches for comprehensive guest management functionality.

pagination.description: Pagination parameters for controlling result sets and page navigation in member queries

search.description:
Search term for filtering members by username, email, or display name using partial matching.

Supports case-insensitive substring search across multiple member fields for comprehensive member discovery and management.

created_after.description: Filter members created after this timestamp for registration date range queries

created_before.description: Filter members created before this timestamp for bounded registration period analysis

filter.description:
Additional filtering options for member search operations beyond basic text search.

Provides date-range filtering capabilities to analyze member registration patterns and platform growth over specific time periods.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for searching and filtering discussion board member accounts.

Provides comprehensive search and filtering capabilities for member management operations throughout the discussion board platform. Supports pagination for efficient handling of large result sets and various filtering options to narrow down member searches based on different criteria.

This schema enables both simple member list retrieval and complex multi-criteria searches, supporting administrative functions like member analytics, account management, and platform growth tracking. The unified pagination pattern ensures consistency with other search operations in the system.

email.description: Member email address used for authentication and communication. Must be unique across all members and serves as the primary contact method for notifications and account recovery. Email updates require re-verification to ensure account security.

password.description: Plain text password for member authentication. Password updates require current password verification and must meet security requirements including minimum length, complexity, and uniqueness constraints. The backend will hash this password before storage.

display_name.description: Optional display name for member profile customization. Provides personalization while maintaining username uniqueness for system operations. Display names can be changed freely without affecting authentication credentials.

bio.description: Optional biography or description for member profile. Allows members to share information about themselves with the community. Bio content is subject to community guidelines and moderation policies.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IUpdate.description:
Update data for modifying member profile information.

This DTO contains fields that can be updated by authenticated members for their own profiles. It excludes immutable fields like id, username, created_at, and system-managed timestamps. All fields are optional to support partial updates where members can modify specific profile attributes without requiring complete profile re-submission.

Security considerations ensure that only the member themselves or authorized administrators can modify profile information. Email and password updates require additional verification steps to prevent unauthorized account access. All updates are validated against database constraints and business rules to maintain data integrity.

This DTO integrates with the discussion_board_members table update operations, providing controlled modification of member profile details while maintaining audit trail and security compliance.

member_id.description: Foreign key reference to the member who owns this session. Provides session ownership tracking without exposing detailed member information in session responses.

ip.description: IP address of the member session connection captured during authentication. Used for security auditing, geographic tracking, and connection pattern analysis to detect suspicious activity.

href.description: Connection URL where the member session was established, representing the current page URL at login time. Used for tracking user navigation patterns and session context.

referrer.description: Referrer URL that directed the member to the session, indicating the previous page before authentication. Provides context for user navigation flow and session initiation patterns.

expired_at.description: Timestamp when the member session expired or was terminated, null if session remains active. Used for session lifecycle management and automatic cleanup of expired sessions.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when the member session was soft deleted, null if session is still active. Supports audit trail preservation while removing active session functionality.

IDiscussionBoardMemberSession.description:
Authentication session entity for member users tracking connection context and session lifecycle.

Represents individual authentication sessions for registered members, capturing detailed connection information including IP address, access URLs, and session timestamps. Each session belongs to a specific member user and maintains authentication state throughout its lifecycle. Sessions provide the foundation for secure member access to discussion board features including post creation, commenting, and content management.

Sessions are used for security auditing, tracking member activity patterns, and troubleshooting connection issues. The session lifecycle includes creation during authentication, updates for connection changes, expiration for security purposes, and soft deletion for audit trail preservation. Session management ensures secure access control while maintaining comprehensive activity logging for administrative oversight.

This entity integrates with the discussion_board_member_sessions table as defined in the Prisma schema, providing comprehensive session management capabilities for the discussion board platform. The session data supports security compliance, user experience optimization, and administrative monitoring requirements.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the member session was last updated.

expired_at.description: Timestamp when the member session expired or was terminated.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when the member session was soft deleted.

IDiscussionBoardMemberSession.ISummary.description:
Summary view of member session for list operations and efficient data transfer.

Provides essential session information with connection context for display in lists and overview operations. Includes only the most critical fields needed for identification and basic context while maintaining accurate representation of the Prisma schema structure.

This summary type is optimized for performance in list operations, reducing data transfer overhead while providing sufficient information for session identification and connection context. The schema accurately reflects all fields from the discussion_board_member_sessions table as defined in the Prisma schema.

Used primarily in administrative interfaces for session management and audit purposes, providing comprehensive session tracking information without unnecessary data overhead.
